statements.t: We focus on providing high quality service to targeted customers with a high density of freight in our operating areas.
We expect to continue to evaluate acquisition candidates presented to us, however, we do not expect to make any significant acquisitions while we are paying down debt.
We believe this has and will continue to improve current supply and demand dynamics in our industry.
We cannot predict what fuel prices will be for the remainder of 2026, but year-to-date fuel expense is our second highest expense behind salaries, wages, and benefits.
We expect to continue to manage and implement fuel strategies that we believe will effectively manage fuel costs.
We expect further favorable pricing changes to happen throughout 2027.
We will continue to further evaluate our driver pay packages.
We expect our ability to attract and retain experienced drivers will continue to be a challenge in the foreseeable future.
We expect fuel prices to remain elevated, compared to historical prices until current conflicts in the Middle East subside and other economic conditions improve the supply of diesel fuel.

As our fuel surcharge agreements do not cover fuel consumed in out-of-route miles, empty miles, and idle time, we expect fuel prices to negatively impact our operating results until fuel prices reduce to the average DOE pricing of 2025.

We anticipate that the average age of our fleet of tractors and trailers will not change significantly by December 31, 2026 as new equipment purchases are largely expected to offset the aging of our existing fleet.
As a result, our insurance and claims expense could likely increase with unfavorable claims experience and will be volatile in future periods.
We expect depreciation expense in 2026 to be approximately $125 million to $130 million.
For the remainder of 2026, we currently expect $9 to $13 million of gains on disposal of property and equipment.
We expect further reductions to interest expense as we continue to pay down the debt.
We intend to continue paying down the CFI debt, while maintaining our regular quarterly dividends and funding our ongoing capital expenditure needs.

While we are paying down the CFI debt, we do not currently expect to declare special dividends, repurchase a significant volume of shares of our common stock, or make significant acquisitions, however we will remain flexible to ensure the best deployment of our capital.

Management believes we will have sufficient cash flows provided by operating activities, proceeds from the sale of used equipment and property, or the ability to refinance the remaining debt, if necessary, prior to maturity.
We expect continued fleet modernization throughout 2026 and beyond.
For the remainder of 2026, we currently anticipate net capital expenditures to be approximately $2 to $5 million and $9 to $13 million of gains on disposal of property and equipment.

While we are paying down the debt, we do not currently expect to repurchase a significant volume of shares of our common stock, however we will remain flexible to ensure the best deployment of our capital.
Management believes we have adequate liquidity to meet our current and projected needs in the foreseeable future.

Management believes we will continue to have significant capital requirements over the long-term, which we may fund with current available cash, cash flows provided by operating activities, proceeds from the sale of used equipment and property, or stock offerings, and to a lesser extent, available capacity on the Credit Facilities.

The improved financial results reflect stronger freight volumes and improved customer pricing resulting from ongoing industry capacity reductions, even though we do not expect the positive impacts of ongoing contract negotiations to be fully reflected in our operating results until 2027.
We expect to rely on our positive cash flows from operations to invest in our fleet of tractors and trailers over the remainder of the year.
We expect to continue to dispose of excess trailers within our fleet as used equipment market conditions improve.
For the remainder of 2026, we currently expect total net capital expenditures to be approximately $2 to $5 million and $9 to $13 million of total gains on disposal of property and equipment.
